prompts.strider:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original conceptual research illustration for a scientist's academic website, one of three visually consistent research thumbnails. Wide landscape composition, approximately 1.65:1 aspect ratio; all essential subjects inside the central 85 percent, generous breathing room, still clear at 350px wide. Style: refined 3D scientific editorial illustration with restrained detail, softly rendered translucent materials, precise believable geometry, gentle ambient occlusion, orthographic three-quarter view, soft studio illumination. Palette consistent with an academic site: warm ivory background #fafaf7, deep forest teal #176253, muted sage, pale blue-green fluid; tiny restrained antique gold highlights. Flat seamless light background, not a framed card. Absolutely no text, labels, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, scale bars, charts, dramatic glow, science-fiction mechanical parts, or medical claims. The illustration is a conceptual depiction inspired by a published study, not an experimental micrograph or a reproduction of the paper figure.
Primary request: Bio-inspired design, specifically the water-strider-inspired miniature magnetoelastic jumping robot in Wang et al., Advanced Science (2023), DOI 10.1002/advs.202207493. Show ONE insect-scale soft robot consisting of EXACTLY FOUR flat slender magnetoelastic silicone ribbon legs joined at a very small central junction, splayed in an X configuration, subtly flexing downward and outward. Dark charcoal-teal particle-filled silicone, no engine, no battery, no eyes, no head, no antennae, no rigid exoskeleton. A serene translucent pale teal water surface across the lower half with four localized surface-tension dimples near the tips of the four legs, delicate concentric ripples and a few tiny droplets suggesting takeoff. Depict the robot at the moment of launching from the water, its four soft legs clear and complete. One subtle short pale gold upward trajectory arc beside the robot can suggest controllable jumping, no arrowheads or text. Communicate biological inspiration, elasticity, surface tension and amphibious jumping through the form and water interaction. Composition should be elegant and mechanically plausible, with the entire four-legged robot and water contacts readable. Do not substitute a six-legged insect, centipede, boat or humanoid.

Primary request: Ciliated robotic system for intravascular applications, CiliaVine, Science Advances (2026), DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aeg3333. The supplied reference image is SCIENTIFIC CONTENT REFERENCE ONLY, not an edit target and not a layout/style template. Create a fresh uncluttered scene focusing on one guidewire-mounted flexible millirobot inside a translucent pale coral blood-vessel segment crossing diagonally across the image. A thin smooth metallic-gray guidewire enters the small central soft cylindrical body. Numerous individually visible flexible tapered soft magnetic cilia are arranged HELICALLY around that body, resembling small curved flexible ribbons radiating outward along a helical vine. The cilia are deep forest teal and gently bend in the fluid; no rigid propeller blades, no hairs like a bottle brush, no long linear row of legs. Show delicate teal streamlines curving around cilia with small local paired recirculating vortices, plus a few tiny gold tracer particles displaced toward the vessel wall. Let the near wall of the vessel be transparent so the device is unobscured. Include at most a few subtle muted coral red blood cells for intravascular context; no clutter, thrombus gore or simulated quantitative results. Communicate remote soft actuation, intravascular deployment and controllable local transport in ONE readable focal composition.

Primary request: Magnetic microrobot swarms for active exploration and reconstruction of vascular networks, Du, Wang et al., Nature Machine Intelligence (2025), DOI 10.1038/s42256-025-01012-y. Show a small three-dimensional branching transparent vascular-channel network with several Y junctions and one branch curving slightly above another, made of translucent pale sage/blue-green tubes. Within two adjacent branches, many TINY charcoal-teal magnetic nanoparticles form dense coherent elongated collective swarms, with individual particle granularity visible at edges, traveling as collectives into branching pathways. No large robot bodies, no cartoon machines, no helix-shaped robots, no gold drug carriers. Delicate dark teal dotted trajectories inside the tubes indicate the actively explored path. Off to the back/right of the same network, integrate a very subtle thin-line teal reconstruction echo of those exact branches with a handful of tiny gold branch nodes, conveying that exploration yields a reconstructed 3D map; keep it minimal and secondary, with no screen, panels, charts, labels or fabricated data. One branch may end at a small muted coral occlusion with the swarm exploring toward it, conceptual only. A clear elegant visual story of collective magnetic particles, branch exploration and network mapping, optimized for a small website thumbnail.
